correctness.rationale: For positive M at rho=1, the positive left Perron functional strictly decreases under F for every nonzero state and has no positive limiting level. Normalized direction contracts to the right Perron vector because all other eigenvalues of M have modulus below one. The scalar Perron projection then satisfies V(t+1)=V(t)-alpha V(t)^2+o(V(t)^2), giving t V(t)->1/alpha and t x(t)->v/alpha by a reciprocal-increment Cesàro argument. Explicit derivative w_i M_ij v_j^2>0 proves cost sensitivity. Standalone exact rational and numerical checks corroborate the derivation without substituting for proof.

value.rationale: Ecological extinction versus persistence threshold data do not quantify the slowing of decay at exact criticality. The result gives a universal, explicit t^{-1} profile for every patch, and an exact monotone sensitivity to nonlinear density-cost parameters that leave linear spectral thresholds invariant. It applies to nonmonotone nonlinear maps and any finite dimension, and distinguishes parametrically arbitrarily different extinction amplitudes in landscapes with identical zero-density growth matrices.
